task.name: Landing evidence is written per run but never indexed, so the substrate answers landed queries from a completion-time snapshot instead
task.story_text:
Landing evidence is written per run as an individual assertion file under the landing
audit directory, each carrying its own `observed_at`. Nothing aggregates those files. The
audit substrate answers landed queries from the flattened `landing_status` column instead,
and that column is populated from a record written at story completion, before a queued
pull request resolves.

The consequence is that any question spanning runs cannot be asked of the substrate at
all, and a reader that asks it of the flattened column receives a pre-resolution snapshot
as though it were an outcome. Absence of an assertion and a recorded non-landing collapse
into the same answer, so "not yet resolved" is indistinguishable from "did not land".

An indexed projection of assertions into the substrate would let landed queries be
answered from the evidence that actually records the event, with the timestamps that
evidence carries. Because evidence is a new artifact beside the run record rather than a
field within it, the projection needs a `SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump and a
`rebuild_from_runs` path — which is why the originating spike placed it outside its own
slice.

This is follow-on 3 of the project-memory publication and landing-evidence spike. Follow-on
4, which re-points the readers that consume the flattened column directly, is sequenced
explicitly after this one and is not in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A landed query answered by the substrate is answered from projected landing evidence
  rather than from the flattened `landing_status` field. Where a run has no assertion, the
  substrate reports its landing state as unresolved. Absence of evidence and recorded
  non-landing are distinct states and stay distinguishable through every reader that
  consumes the projection.

- Each projected assertion retains its recorded `observed_at` together with the run
  identity it belongs to, so the interval between a run's own recorded timing and its
  landing is derivable from the substrate alone for any run holding both endpoints. Where
  either endpoint is absent the row is reported as unresolved. No endpoint is defaulted,
  imputed, or substituted from a neighbouring run.

- `SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and `rebuild_from_runs` reconstructs the projection
  from the canonical assertion files, so a substrate rebuilt from scratch answers landing
  queries identically to one built incrementally.

- The projection is defined over an assertion's recorded fields rather than over the set of
  values observed so far. An assertion carrying a landing mode, observer or target branch
  not present in the current corpus projects on the same terms as one that is; an
  unrecognised value is projected and surfaced, never filtered out or mapped onto a known
  one.

- The readers that consume the flattened column directly are unchanged by this work and
  continue to read `landing_status` as they do today.

## Example

The repository currently holds 14 landing assertions. One of them records:

```
run_id        05193a8cf1c8       slug          issue-2755
observed_at   2026-08-26T06:18:39.709609+00:00
landing_mode  merge-pr           carrier_ref   #2756
observer      sprint.queued-pr   target_branch release/v0.16
```

All 14 carry a real `observed_at`, and every one must remain queryable after the
projection: 12 were observed by `sprint.queued-pr` and 2 by `forge.reconcile`, all with
landing mode `merge-pr` onto `release/v0.16`.

Against that, 224 recorded story specs carry a flattened landing block, and all 224 read
`landing_path: fresh-merge  merged: False  pr_merged_at: null` — the completion-time
snapshot, not the outcome. Two separate operator sessions queried the flattened blocks,
found no timestamps, and concluded that finished-to-landed latency is recorded nowhere in
the artifacts. It is recorded, in the 14 assertions above. Nothing could aggregate it, and
the reader that was available answered from the snapshot instead.

handoff.summary: Added a first-class landing-evidence projection to the audit substrate. SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 12→13 with two new TEXT-only tables (landing_assertions keyed by run_id, landing_attempts keyed by (run_id, artifact_name)) carrying each artifact's recorded fields verbatim — no CHECK constraints on landing_mode, observer, target_branch or outcome, so unrecognised values project unfiltered. audit_storage.sync_landing_evidence scans landing_evidence_read_dirs (canonical tree first, then memory-staging), validates payloads with is_landing_assertion/is_landing_attempt, and rewrites both tables wholesale when a (relpath, mtime) fingerprint over the evidence tree changes; malformed artifacts are skipped so a corrupt file leaves its run unresolved rather than raising. It runs on create_or_open, on require_substrate (both the fresh-rebuild and the already-present paths), and forced at the end of rebuild_from_runs, so a scratch rebuild and an incrementally maintained substrate converge by construction. It is deliberately NOT wired into _native_rows_are_stale: that predicate's only remedy is the destructive rebuild_from_runs, which drops readiness_events, shape_verdict_events, inline_remediation_events and the triage tables, and landing observations arrive on every landed story. A schema-version bump clears the projection fingerprint so an existing substrate re-projects on first open without operator action. The read model gains landing_states / landing_state_for_run / landed_run_ids_in_substrate / landing_projection_status, over a single SQL view that UNIONs run ids from audit_records and both evidence tables (so evidence for a run with no indexed record is still queryable) and left-joins audit_records only for run timing. has_review_approve_in_substrate(require_landed=True) now filters on an EXISTS against landing_assertions instead of a.landing_status; latest_run_outcome_in_substrate is untouched and documented as the deferred flattened-column reader. landing_evidence.py gained OPEN_ATTEMPT_OUTCOMES / RESOLVED_NON_LANDING_OUTCOMES so the SQL reader and the filesystem reader draw the same line, with landing_state refactored onto them.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A landed query answered by the substrate is answered from projected landing evidence rather than from the flattened landing_status field. Where a run has no assertion, the substrate reports its landing state as unresolved. Absence of evidence and recorded non-landing are distinct states and stay distinguishable through every reader that consumes the projection.
acceptance_criteria.notes: has_review_approve_in_substrate(require_landed=True) filters on landing_assertions; landing_states/landing_state_for_run return 'landed'/'not_landed'/'unresolved' as distinct string values (not a nullable boolean), so no consumer can collapse them by accident. A run with no evidence, and a run whose last attempt is queued/unknown, are unresolved; only an enumerated resolved outcome (refused/failed/timeout/closed) yields not_landed. Covered by TestAbsenceIsNotFailure, including a test asserting the SQL answer matches landing_evidence.landing_state run-for-run.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each projected assertion retains its recorded observed_at together with the run identity it belongs to, so the interval between a run's own recorded timing and its landing is derivable from the substrate alone for any run holding both endpoints. Where either endpoint is absent the row is reported as unresolved. No endpoint is defaulted, imputed, or substituted from a neighbouring run.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Each row carries run_id, the assertion's own observed_at, and run_started_at/run_finished_at from audit_records, plus a landing_interval dict that is {state: resolved, seconds: N} only when both endpoints parse. Otherwise state is unresolved, seconds is None, and missing_endpoints names which endpoint was absent. TestObservedAtAndIntervals pins both directions plus a test that a run without evidence does not inherit a neighbouring run's timestamp.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped and rebuild_from_runs reconstructs the projection from the canonical assertion files, so a substrate rebuilt from scratch answers landing queries identically to one built incrementally.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Bumped to 13. rebuild_from_runs calls sync_landing_evidence(force=True) over the same artifacts the incremental path reads. TestRebuildParity asserts the full landing_states mapping is byte-identical before and after a rebuild over a mixed corpus (assertion, open attempt, resolved attempt, no evidence, and an attempt later superseded by an assertion).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The projection is defined over an assertion's recorded fields rather than over the set of values observed so far. An assertion carrying a landing mode, observer or target branch not present in the current corpus projects on the same terms as one that is; an unrecognised value is projected and surfaced, never filtered out or mapped onto a known one.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Columns are plain TEXT with no CHECK constraint and no allow-list in _text_or_none, which stores the recorded value verbatim. TestUnrecognisedValuesProjectVerbatim round-trips landing_mode='teleport', observer='some.future.observer', target_branch='experiment/not-a-release-line', asserts two distinct unknown modes stay two values rather than one bucket, and inspects the DDL directly to prove no CHECK was added.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The readers that consume the flattened column directly are unchanged by this work and continue to read landing_status as they do today.
acceptance_criteria.notes: latest_run_outcome_in_substrate and its downstream merge-evidence consumers are unchanged and return the stored column verbatim, including where the projection disagrees because the work landed after the record was written — pinned by TestFlattenedColumnReadersUnchanged, which is the follow-on-4 boundary guard. The one exception is deliberate and mandated by AC1: has_review_approve_in_substrate is simultaneously the landed query and a landing_status consumer, and the approved plan re-points it. The plan reviewer flagged this AC1/AC5 overlap as P2 and adjudicated it the same way. Marked PARTIAL rather than MET because that reader did change; the module comment on the changed helper states the split explicitly.

story_deviations: Modified six existing tests that seeded landing_status='landed' and asserted the landed query accepted it (test_coord_audit.py x1, test_sprint_resume.py x3, test_sprint_reexec_reconcile.py x1, test_sprint_runner.py x1). They are the direct subject of AC1 — each now publishes a real landing assertion via a new shared helper tests/landing_evidence_test_helpers.py, matching what a real landing writes. One new test was added alongside the coord_audit one proving the reverse: a flattened 'landed' with no evidence is now refused.
Updated docs/plans/2598-project-memory-publication-spike.md to mark follow-on 3 shipped and record the operator consequence, and corrected its 'Not changed: SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION' note.
deferred_items: OPERATOR RISK, not deferred work: this repo's substrate holds 75 records with landing_status='landed' against 64 evidence artifacts. Runs whose landing predates evidence now read as unresolved, so sprint/dag.py:_has_prior_review_approve will not recognise them as merged until reconciliation publishes an assertion. Reconciliation runs at sprint startup so this self-closes over a sprint, but expect one noisy pass on a repo with long pre-evidence history. Documented in the spike doc's follow-on 3.

open_readonly cannot sync the projection (it may not write), so it answers from the last-indexed state. Contract decided explicitly rather than left implicit: landing_projection_status exposes assertion/attempt counts, synced_at, and the source-artifact count the index was built from, so a caller can tell 'not re-indexed' from 'never landed'. Documented in the open_readonly docstring and pinned by TestReadOnlyOpeningContract.
Follow-on 4 (re-pointing cli/audits.py, cli/sprint_digest.py, coordinator/issue_cost.py and latest_run_outcome_in_substrate off the flattened column) remains out of scope, per the spec.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 must not handle landing-evidence staleness by blindly entering require_substrate's existing destructive rebuild_from_runs branch. That rebuild preserves legacy audit_records and shape_skip_events, but drops non-reconstructible readiness_events, shape_verdict_events, inline_remediation_events, and triage tables.
  Suggestion: Refresh only the landing projection in place when evidence changes, or preserve every non-reconstructible table across the rebuild; add a regression proving an evidence refresh does not erase those rows.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk (plan's own risk 2): open_readonly (audit_storage.py:960) cannot repair or populate a stale landing projection, so any read-only surface — forge explain, and any future operator query — can serve an empty or outdated projection while the incremental path is healthy. The plan's mitigation only covers paths that already call require_substrate; it names no behaviour for the read-only path beyond 'document test expectations'. No acceptance criterion depends on it today (the only reader Step 3 re-points, has_review_approve, goes through require_substrate), so it does not block.
  Suggestion: Decide the read-only contract explicitly in Step 3: either surface the projection's staleness (e.g. an unresolved/stale marker derived from stored source_path/source_mtime) rather than silently returning fewer landed rows, or document in the read-model docstring that read-only openings answer from the last-indexed projection and point at forge audits rebuild. Add one Step 4 test pinning whichever choice is made.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] AC1 ('answered from projected landing evidence') and AC5 ('readers that consume the flattened column are unchanged') both arguably reach has_review_approve_in_substrate, since it is simultaneously the landed query and a direct landing_status consumer. The plan resolves this by re-pointing has_review_approve and freezing latest_run_outcome, which is the reading that makes AC1 non-empty, but it is an interpretation the review of the resulting diff will have to re-derive.
  Suggestion: State the split in a docstring or module comment on the changed helper: has_review_approve_in_substrate is the landed query (AC1, re-pointed here); latest_run_outcome_in_substrate and its downstream merge-evidence consumers are the flattened-column readers deferred to follow-on 4.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.1-pro-preview-api] The plan states 'make require_substrate treat landing-evidence source changes as substrate staleness so an incrementally maintained substrate and a scratch rebuild converge'. In require_substrate, staleness strictly triggers rebuild_from_runs(project_root), which drops and rebuilds the entire database from scratch by parsing every historical run. This breaks the premise of an 'incrementally maintained substrate' and causes a massive performance regression every time a single story lands. Instead of triggering full staleness rebuilds for landing evidence, add an incremental sync function (e.g., _sync_landing_evidence) that scans for unindexed evidence files and INSERTs them. Call this during require_substrate for fast updates. Additionally, call this logic in the schema migration block so existing substrates upgrade seamlessly without a manual rebuild.

plan_finding_registry.description: Step 2 must not handle landing-evidence staleness by blindly entering require_substrate's existing destructive rebuild_from_runs branch. That rebuild preserves legacy audit_records and shape_skip_events, but drops non-reconstructible readiness_events, shape_verdict_events, inline_remediation_events, and triage tables.

Carried risk (plan's own risk 2): open_readonly (audit_storage.py:960) cannot repair or populate a stale landing projection, so any read-only surface — forge explain, and any future operator query — can serve an empty or outdated projection while the incremental path is healthy. The plan's mitigation only covers paths that already call require_substrate; it names no behaviour for the read-only path beyond 'document test expectations'. No acceptance criterion depends on it today (the only reader Step 3 re-points, has_review_approve, goes through require_substrate), so it does not block.

AC1 ('answered from projected landing evidence') and AC5 ('readers that consume the flattened column are unchanged') both arguably reach has_review_approve_in_substrate, since it is simultaneously the landed query and a direct landing_status consumer. The plan resolves this by re-pointing has_review_approve and freezing latest_run_outcome, which is the reading that makes AC1 non-empty, but it is an interpretation the review of the resulting diff will have to re-derive.

The plan states 'make require_substrate treat landing-evidence source changes as substrate staleness so an incrementally maintained substrate and a scratch rebuild converge'. In require_substrate, staleness strictly triggers rebuild_from_runs(project_root), which drops and rebuilds the entire database from scratch by parsing every historical run. This breaks the premise of an 'incrementally maintained substrate' and causes a massive performance regression every time a single story lands. Instead of triggering full staleness rebuilds for landing evidence, add an incremental sync function (e.g., _sync_landing_evidence) that scans for unindexed evidence files and INSERTs them. Call this during require_substrate for fast updates. Additionally, call this logic in the schema migration block so existing substrates upgrade seamlessly without a manual rebuild.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Add a first-class landing-evidence projection to the audit substrate, populated from canonical landing evidence artifacts and queried by landed-only substrate reads. Keep the legacy flattened landing_status column and its direct readers intact for the explicitly sequenced follow-on.

steps.description: Add substrate storage for projected landing evidence
steps.details: Bump SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION from 12 to 13. Extend _SCHEMA and _apply_schema with TEXT-only projection tables/indexes for landing assertions and recorded landing attempts, keyed by run_id/source artifact as appropriate and carrying observed_at, landing_mode, carrier_ref, carrier_kind, observer, target_branch, outcome for attempts, source_path/source_mtime, and raw_json. Do not constrain landing_mode, observer, or target_branch to known values.

steps.description: Populate and refresh the projection from canonical evidence artifacts
steps.details: Add storage-side projection helpers that scan landing_evidence_read_dirs(project_root), validate payloads with is_landing_assertion/is_landing_attempt, and rewrite projection rows from the recorded artifact fields without consulting audit_records.landing_status. Make rebuild_from_runs rebuild this projection after native and preserved run records are loaded, and make require_substrate treat landing-evidence source changes as substrate staleness so an incrementally maintained substrate and a scratch rebuild converge.

Add read-model SELECT helpers over the projection that report landed, not_landed, and unresolved distinctly, include run_id plus recorded observed_at, and join audit_records only to expose run timing endpoints when present. Update has_review_approve_in_substrate so require_landed=True filters through the projected positive assertion rows instead of a.landing_status. Leave latest_run_outcome_in_substrate and other direct landing_status consumers unchanged.

steps.description: Cover projection behavior and rebuild parity with tests
steps.details: Add focused substrate tests proving a run with flattened landing_status unset or false is treated as landed when a valid .landed.json assertion exists, a run with no evidence is unresolved, a resolved failed/refused/timeout/closed attempt is not_landed, unknown assertion field values round-trip unchanged, observed_at and run timing endpoints are queryable without defaults, and rebuild_from_runs produces the same landing projection as the incremental/stale-refresh path. Adjust boundary tests only for new read-model exports while preserving the storage/read split.

Add or update assertions showing latest_run_outcome_in_substrate still returns the stored landing_status column exactly as before, even when the projection disagrees because later evidence landed. This guards the follow-on-4 boundary.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A landed query answered by the substrate is answered from projected landing evidence rather than from the flattened landing_status field. Where a run has no assertion, the substrate reports its landing state as unresolved. Absence of evidence and recorded non-landing are distinct states and stay distinguishable through every reader that consumes the projection.

Each projected assertion retains its recorded observed_at together with the run identity it belongs to, so the interval between a run's own recorded timing and its landing is derivable from the substrate alone for any run holding both endpoints. Where either endpoint is absent the row is reported as unresolved. No endpoint is defaulted, imputed, or substituted from a neighbouring run.

SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped and rebuild_from_runs reconstructs the projection from the canonical assertion files, so a substrate rebuilt from scratch answers landing queries identically to one built incrementally.

The projection is defined over an assertion's recorded fields rather than over the set of values observed so far. An assertion carrying a landing mode, observer or target branch not present in the current corpus projects on the same terms as one that is; an unrecognised value is projected and surfaced, never filtered out or mapped onto a known one.
The readers that consume the flattened column directly are unchanged by this work and continue to read landing_status as they do today.

risks.description: The spec emphasizes assertion files, but the absence-vs-recorded-non-landing criterion requires a source for recorded non-landings.
risks.mitigation: Use existing landing_evidence.py semantics: positive .landed.json assertions drive landed queries, and .attempt-*.json outcomes drive not_landed versus unresolved state without reading landing_status.

risks.description: Read-only substrate openings cannot repair stale projections.
risks.mitigation: Keep open_readonly read-only; make normal runtime paths that already call require_substrate refresh stale landing evidence, and document test expectations around that boundary.
